questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which OOP principle allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method already defined in its parent class?
questions.explanation: Method overriding allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method declared in its superclass.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used by a class to inherit from another class in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword establishes an inheritance relationship between classes.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used by a class to use an interface in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'implements' keyword is used by classes to implement interface contracts.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Starting in Java 8, can interfaces contain default methods with concrete implementations?

options.A: No, interface methods must all be abstract
options.D: Only private methods were allowed in Java 8

questions.explanation: Java 8 introduced default methods in interfaces to allow adding new capabilities without breaking backward compatibility.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which of the following is true about abstract classes in Java?

options.A: An abstract class can be directly instantiated with 'new'
options.B: An abstract class cannot contain constructors
options.C: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly
options.D: All methods in an abstract class must be abstract

questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated directly with 'new'; they must be extended by concrete subclasses.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What type of polymorphism is achieved through Method Overloading?
questions.explanation: Method overloading is resolved by the compiler based on method signatures (compile-time/static polymorphism).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What type of polymorphism is achieved through Method Overriding?
questions.explanation: Method overriding is resolved at runtime based on the actual object type (run-time/dynamic polymorphism).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Collection interface allows fast lookup by key and does not allow duplicate keys?
questions.explanation: Map stores key-value pairs where keys are unique.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of ArrayList over a standard Java array?

options.B: ArrayList automatically resizes dynamically as elements are added
options.D: ArrayList elements are fixed in size

questions.explanation: ArrayList grows dynamically when elements are added beyond its current capacity.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: How does HashMap handle key collisions in Java 8 and later when a bucket capacity exceeds a threshold?

options.B: Converts the bucket from a linked list to a balanced tree (Red-Black tree)
options.C: Replaces old value with new value automatically

questions.explanation: When a bucket linked list exceeds 8 elements (and total table capacity >= 64), Java 8 converts it to a balanced red-black tree.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is Type Erasure in Java Generics?

options.A: Removing generic type information at compile time so bytecode maintains backward compatibility
options.B: Erasing unused objects from heap memory
options.C: Casting primitive types to wrapper classes

questions.explanation: Type erasure removes generic type parameters during compilation, inserting necessary casts for type safety.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which wildcard syntax allows accepting a List of Integer or any of its superclasses?
questions.explanation: <? super Integer> specifies a lower-bounded wildcard accepting Integer or its superclasses.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens if a recursive function does not have a proper base condition?
questions.explanation: Infinite recursion exhausts call stack space, leading to StackOverflowError.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which class in java.nio.file package provides utility methods to read all lines from a text file conveniently?
questions.explanation: java.nio.file.Files provides static methods like Files.readAllLines().

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
questions.explanation: IOException is a checked exception derived from Exception, requiring explicit try-catch or throws.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What class is the root of the exception hierarchy in Java?
questions.explanation: java.lang.Throwable is the superclass of all errors and exceptions in Java.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which statement accurately describes a Functional Interface in Java?

options.B: An interface with exactly one abstract method
options.C: An interface containing only static methods
options.D: An interface with multiple abstract methods

questions.explanation: A functional interface contains exactly one abstract method (annotated optionally with @FunctionalInterface).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which standard functional interface takes one argument and returns a boolean?
questions.explanation: Predicate<T> defines boolean test(T t).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which functional interface takes no parameters and produces/returns a result?
questions.explanation: Supplier<T> defines T get() which accepts no arguments and produces a result.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Stream operation is terminal and reduces elements to a single value or performs a side-effect?
questions.explanation: forEach is a terminal operation that triggers stream processing; filter, map, and sorted are intermediate.

questions.subject: Java
questions.explanation: The filter keeps even numbers (2, 4), so count() returns 2.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What does the Stream map() method do?

options.A: Filters elements based on a condition
options.B: Transforms each element into another element using a function
options.C: Sorts the elements of a stream
options.D: Groups elements into a Map object

questions.explanation: map() applies a mapping function to transform elements in the stream.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Encapsulation is best demonstrated by which of the following practices?

options.A: Making fields public for direct access
options.B: Making instance variables private and providing public getter and setter methods

questions.explanation: Hiding internal data behind private access modifiers and exposing safe access via public methods embodies encapsulation.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Can a class in Java extend multiple concrete classes directly (Multiple Inheritance)?

options.D: Yes, if both parent classes are abstract

questions.explanation: Java does not support multiple class inheritance to avoid ambiguity (the diamond problem).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the super keyword used for in a constructor of a child class?

options.C: To reference the child class instance

questions.explanation: super(...) invokes the constructor of the direct parent class.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Set implementation in Java maintains elements in insertion order?
questions.explanation: LinkedHashSet maintains a doubly-linked list running through its entries to preserve insertion order.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Set implementation automatically sorts its elements in natural ascending order?
questions.explanation: TreeSet is backed by a Red-Black tree and stores elements in natural sorted order or via a custom Comparator.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is a custom unchecked exception in Java?
questions.explanation: Unchecked exceptions extend RuntimeException (or Throwable/Error, but custom exceptions extend RuntimeException).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the correct syntax for a lambda expression taking two integers 'a' and 'b' and returning their sum?
questions.explanation: (a, b) -> a + b is valid Java lambda syntax.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which method is used to convert a Stream back into a List in Java 16 or later?
questions.explanation: Java 16 introduced Stream.toList() as an unmodifiable convenience method.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Can an abstract class have concrete (implemented) methods in Java?

options.A: No, all methods in an abstract class must be abstract
options.B: Yes, an abstract class can contain both abstract and concrete methods
options.C: Only if the class is declared static
options.D: Only if methods are marked final

questions.explanation: Abstract classes can feature both fully implemented methods and abstract methods.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Can an interface have instance fields (non-static, non-final fields)?

options.B: No, fields in interfaces are implicitly public static final

questions.explanation: All fields declared in interfaces are implicitly public, static, and final.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using Generics in Java collections?

options.B: Compile-time type checking and elimination of explicit type casting

questions.explanation: Generics enforce type safety at compile time, eliminating manual casting and preventing ClassCastException.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Java class is best suited for writing low-level binary data to a file?
questions.explanation: FileOutputStream writes raw bytes/binary data to files.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which class is designed for reading characters and text efficiently with buffering?
questions.explanation: BufferedReader reads text efficiently from a character-input stream by buffering characters.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens if a catch block catches a broad Exception before a specific SubException block?

options.B: Compilation error occurs due to unreachable code

questions.explanation: The Java compiler reports an error because the lower catch block for SubException would be unreachable.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens when a subclass object calls an overridden method using a superclass reference? (e.g., Animal a = new Dog(); a.makeSound();)
questions.explanation: Dynamic method dispatch invokes the implementation corresponding to the actual object type (Dog) at runtime.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which interface does Map extend in the Java Collections Framework?

options.C: Map does not extend Collection interface

questions.explanation: Map is part of the Java Collections Framework, but it does NOT extend Collection or Iterable.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the underlying data structure of dynamic sizing for ArrayList?
questions.explanation: ArrayList uses a contiguous internal array that expands when capacity is reached.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: In recursion, what is the 'base case'?

options.A: The line where function calls itself
options.B: The terminating condition that stops further recursive calls
options.C: The initial value passed to the root call

questions.explanation: The base case prevents infinite recursion by providing a stopping condition.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which concept refers to binding data members and methods into a single unit?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods together and protects internal state.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the difference between intermediate and terminal operations in Java Streams?

options.A: Intermediate operations trigger stream processing; terminal operations return streams
options.B: Intermediate operations return a new Stream and are lazy; terminal operations produce a result or side-effect
options.C: Terminal operations can be chained together

questions.explanation: Intermediate operations return streams lazily; terminal operations execute the pipeline.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which functional interface accepts two arguments and returns no result?
questions.explanation: BiConsumer<T, U> accepts two input arguments and performs an operation without returning a result.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is a Method Reference in Java?

options.A: A pointer to C++ native code
options.B: A compact lambda expression for invoking an existing method by name (e.g., System.out::println)
options.D: An abstract method in an interface

questions.explanation: Method references provide readable, concise syntax using :: to refer directly to existing methods.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the key difference between Vector and ArrayList?

options.A: Vector is dynamic; ArrayList is fixed
options.B: Vector methods are synchronized (thread-safe); ArrayList is not
options.C: ArrayList allows duplicate values; Vector does not
options.D: Vector is faster than ArrayList in single-threaded environments

questions.explanation: Vector synchronizes its operations, making it thread-safe but slower than unsynchronized ArrayList.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which principle of OOP focuses on showing only essential features and hiding internal complexity?
questions.explanation: Abstraction hides background implementation details and shows essential features.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Can an interface extend multiple interfaces in Java?

options.A: No, interfaces can only extend one interface
options.B: Yes, using comma-separated list of interfaces
options.C: Only if all interfaces have no default methods
options.D: Interfaces implement other interfaces, not extend

questions.explanation: Interfaces support multiple inheritance from other interfaces (e.g. interface C extends A, B).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is try-with-resources introduced in Java 7?

options.A: A try block that automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable
options.B: A try block with multiple catch clauses
options.C: A try block that rethrows exceptions automatically
options.D: A try block for managing memory allocation

questions.explanation: Try-with-resources ensures that each resource implementing AutoCloseable is closed at the end of the statement.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What does the symbol <?> represent in Java Generics?
questions.explanation: <?> represents an unbounded wildcard, standing for any unknown type.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which class provides static utility methods to sort, search, and reverse Collections?
questions.explanation: java.util.Collections contains static helper methods operating on Collections.
